title: 1965 AHSME Problem 26
statement: For the numbers \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) \(d,\) \(e\) define \(m\) to be the arithmetic mean of all five numbers; \(k\) to be the arithmetic mean of \(a\) and \(b;\) \(l\) to be the arithmetic mean of \(c,\) \(d,\) and \(e;\) and \(p\) to be the arithmetic mean of \(k\) and \(l.\) Then, no matter how \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) \(d,\) \(e\) are chosen, we shall always have:

solutions.text:
We have \[m=\frac{2k+3l}{5}\] and \[p=\frac{k+l}{2},\] so \(m-p=\frac{l-k}{10}.\) This difference may be positive, zero, or negative depending on the chosen numbers. None of the first four relations always holds.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Express \(m\) in terms of the subgroup means \(k\) and \(l\)
